scope: Repair the existing regular Rust kernel ARP/RX owner. Recovery0.1.68 has an independent correction. No module/API/ABI change.
root_cause: After30s the next-hop ARP cache expires. Synchronous resolution while the serialized RX protocol consumer sends a TCP ACK prevents it from consuming the already queued ARP reply. Regular SMP kernels also dispatch frames on net-rx-ap, not just the BSP net-rx maintenance/poll task.

implementation.workers: Private predicate reuses exact current task ID/generation matching for BSP and AP workers. Existing BSP-only public query/poll semantics remain unchanged.
implementation.miss: On an RX-worker cache miss, request at most once per adapter per500ms and immediately return existing Busy. Original TCP owner retains unsent ACK/FIN/retransmit work for another activation.
implementation.ownership: Protect only resident pacing/counters with the short network owner. Driver/protocol request callback runs after release. No recursive poll, idle or ARP wait in either RX worker.
implementation.reset: Init clears Metadata; owned ARP flush clears all adapter pacing deadlines.
implementation.ordinary_callers: Original bounded3-attempt resolver, route/cache hits and driver errors retained; reject an invalid adapter before indexing.

source_proof.boundaries: Actual bodies; mock clock, adapter admission, ARP cache, native current task identity/scheduler and short metadata guard; actual BSP/AP worker predicate bodies included. Peer callbacks record any execution under the owner.

artifacts.versions: Kernel0.1.460 and release0.89.59; module versions unchanged because module artifacts are unchanged.

temporary_host_cases.source: Actual resolver/cache-flush/reset and actual BSP/AP predicate bodies; no product implementation rewritten in the fixture.
temporary_host_cases.boundaries: Mock clock, adapter/cache, native task identity/scheduler and network admission. Assert all peer callbacks execute outside admission. This is a source-level boundary proof, not a host NIC test.
cases: Per-adapter500ms pacing and exact boundary; init/flush reset
Cached reply resolves without another request
Driver failure and invalid adapter preserve ownership/counters
Ordinary caller synchronous reply and3-timeout behavior
Both BSP/AP exact identities; stale generations, foreign and absent current tasks

routed_transfer.method: Identical temporary SDK R4X streams64MB into a hash sink, no target file. Server cap1MB/s, max_retries0. Off-subnet SSH prevents LAN traffic from refreshing router ARP. Private images use exact before/final normal product ELFs with verified BOOT readback.
routed_transfer.before_stop: Bounded110s host watchdog; no successful completion. Last observed progress26,315,936 bytes, about956B/s;216 additional ARP resolve timeouts and72 additional pending drops.
routed_transfer.after_result: Complete64MB in64047 kernel ticks at1000Hz; correct SHA256. Both30s cache expirations cross without throughput collapse; zero ARP resolve timeouts/pending drops and zero NIC backend errors.
routed_transfer.generic_counters: Busy/backpressure and TCP drop counters are not zero (post-transfer TX Busy197, TCP rx_drops35); no general zero-loss claim. ARP/NIC error counts are reported separately.

failed_candidate.reason: Initial BSP-only worker predicate missed the real AP protocol consumer. Targeted witness failed and was preserved; predicate corrected to include AP before final build/tests. No STANDARD on that candidate.

standard.owner_reconstruction: entire original export, 30 raw samples / 5 metrics / 6 scores, fixed original reference
standard.server_remaining: Claim/import of these unchanged original bytes plus complete GET and independent server scoring validation.

validation.archive: ExFiles/Reports/Network/KernelArp08959/; original logs, pcaps, before/final/failed ELFs and metadata, source snapshots and SHA256.json. Temporary helpers stay under Temp/KernelArp08959/.
validation.limits: One targeted KVM4/VIRTNET route witness, not a hardware/CDN throughput campaign. The first cold-cache forwarded SSH banner timed out in all three fixtures; subsequent off-subnet sessions worked. This evidence does not establish initial-handshake reliability. NETWORK LIMIT is scoped; STANDARD has no TCP workload. OssiPC installation and new Full/Slim GitHub binary releases are outside this subversion.

standard_previous.interpretation: Descriptive single-run comparison only, including lower values. No performance parity or causal attribution; STANDARD uses no network. No repeat for better scores.

test_policy: Reuse existing NETWORK LIMIT; six bounded temporary source-derived cases only, no new permanent gate or broad catalog. Exactly one final STANDARD Suite3/SMP4; preserve original export/reference/context/artifacts and validate full reconstruction. Server import uses the explicit local completion exception.
